newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends at 35.65/66, dlr demand seen firm.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends at 35.65/66, dlr demand seen firm.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.650/657 per dollar on Tuesday against the 35.64/65 opening on continued dollar demand from eastern India, dealers said.
The rupee came under pressure soon after the market opened, slipping to 35.66/67 in early inter-bank trade, they said.
The day's range was 35.6450-35.6825 per dollar.
A dealer at a foreign bank said the market was long on dollars and was largely taking care of the demand.
A $50 million forward dollar sale on Tuesday threatened to tilt the balance but the Reserve Bank of India promptly stepped in to avert the rupee's appreciation, a bank dealer said.

Another dealer said the buying behaviour of the major participant showed he needed to buy at any rate, indicating a buching of import demand, which looked like continuing till the last day of this month.

The six-month forward premia dipped to 1.20 rupee level on Tuesday. The deputy general manager (forex) at a textile company, who earlier forecast the premia slipping to this level, said the forwards could see further softening.
